name: dalobaby
description: Dalo Baby's baby food guide, first foods, solids readiness check, nap plan, milk calculator, development milestones and sleep, solids and breast milk guides, from dalofamilyapps.com.

interface.longDescription:
Dalo Baby answers everyday baby feeding and sleep questions with the guides and tools at dalofamilyapps.com.

What it does:
- Baby food guide: for 990+ generic foods, how to prepare, cut and serve them by age group (6–9 months, 9–18 months, 18+ months), with an allergen risk and a choking hazard rating (1–5). Foods that should not be given at an age, such as honey before 12 months, say so first.
- Gentle first foods: a hand-picked list of soft, single-ingredient, low-allergen, low-choking-risk foods to start solids with.
- Solids readiness check: the baby's age and six WHO/AAP readiness signs give ready, almost or not yet, with a sign-by-sign breakdown.
- Nap plan: from the baby's age and this morning's wake time, today's naps and bedtime with the wake windows and sleep totals for the age.
- Milk amount: how much formula or breast milk a baby needs a day and per feed, from AAP and NHS guidance, with signs it's enough and signs worth a call.
- Development milestones: what most babies do from 0 to 24 months in four areas (cognitive, language, movement, social-emotional), based on the CDC's "Learn the Signs. Act Early." checklists, with when to talk to your pediatrician.
- Guides: sourced, editorially reviewed guides on baby sleep (sleep training methods, nap transitions, wake windows), starting solids (baby-led weaning, allergens, gagging vs choking) and breast milk (pumping, paced bottle feeding, freezer stash), with key takeaways and numbered sources.

Who it is for: parents and caregivers of babies and toddlers up to 3 years. Available in English, Spanish, French and Danish.

Limitations: Dalo Baby is general information for healthy, full-term babies, not medical advice, diagnosis or treatment. It does not handle allergic reactions, choking or illness (call emergency services or your doctor), and it covers generic foods, not branded products. A baby's own doctor or health visitor always comes first. No account is needed and nothing you send is stored.
defaultPrompt: Can my 7 month old eat strawberries? How should I cut them?
My baby is 7 months and woke at 6:30. When should she nap today?
How much formula does my 3 month old need? She weighs 13 lb.

positive.description: Food by age: whether and how to serve a food to a baby of a given age.
positive.prompt: Can my 7 month old eat strawberries? How should I cut them?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_food (food: strawberries, age_months: 7). The card shows Strawberry with allergen risk 2/5 (Low) and choking hazard 4/5 (High), then the guide's 6–9 month text: mashed or puréed, or a whole very large berry held by the stem; no whole small berries or thick slices. 'Read more' expands every age group. The reply is short, does not invent a start age, and links https://dalofamilyapps.com/learn/food/strawberry.

positive.description: Solids readiness: the six WHO/AAP readiness signs give ready, almost or not yet.
positive.prompt: Is my 6 month old ready for solids? She sits with a little help, holds her head up, doesn't push food out with her tongue, reaches for my plate and puts toys in her mouth, but can't hold food yet.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls check_solids_readiness (age_months: 6, five signs true, grasps_food false). The card says 'Ready' (5 of 6 signs, all three safety signs present) with the sign-by-sign breakdown and gentle first foods (avocado, sweet potato, butternut squash, banana…). Links the result page https://dalofamilyapps.com/tools/solids-readiness-quiz/r/6-v.

positive.description: Nap plan: today's naps and bedtime from the baby's age and this morning's wake time.
positive.prompt: My baby is 7 months and woke at 6:30. When should she nap today?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls build_nap_schedule (age_months: 7, wake_time: '6:30'). The card shows three naps (8:45–10:15 AM, 12:45–2:15 PM, 4:45–5:15 PM) and a 7:30 PM bedtime, wake windows 2h 15m–2h 30m, 3h 30m day sleep, 11–12h night sleep, and a note on the coming 3-to-2 nap transition. Links the full plan https://dalofamilyapps.com/tools/wake-window-calculator/r/7-390.

positive.description: Milk amount: how much formula or breast milk a baby needs a day and per feed.
positive.prompt: How much formula does my 3 month old need? She weighs 13 lb.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls milk_amount (milk: formula, age_months: 3, weight_lb: 13). The card shows 27–31 oz a day (typical 31 oz), per feed 6 oz × 5, 5 oz × 6 or 4.5 oz × 7, the AAP 2.5 fl oz per pound note, signs it is enough and signs worth a call to the doctor. Amounts stay in ounces. Links https://dalofamilyapps.com/tools/milk-volume-calculator/r/f5897-3.

positive.description: Sourced guide: a how-to question on baby sleep, solids or breast milk answered from a Dalo Baby guide.
positive.prompt: How does the Ferber method work?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_guide (guide: 'ferber method'). The card shows 'The Ferber method: intervals, timeline and what the evidence shows' with its key takeaways (graduated extinction, AASM review of 52 studies, cortisol trial, five-year follow-up); 'Read the guide' expands the sections, FAQs, numbered sources and disclaimer. The reply summarises without repeating the card and links https://dalofamilyapps.com/learn/sleep/ferber-method.

negative.description: Emergency. No tool: the reply tells the user to call emergency services now, before anything else.
negative.prompt: My baby is choking on a grape right now, what do I do?

negative.description: Allergic reaction happening now. No tool (get_food is not for reactions): the reply tells the user to call their doctor or emergency services now.
negative.prompt: My 8 month old got hives and a swollen lip after eating egg. What should I do?

negative.description: Branded product. No tool: Dalo Baby covers generic foods and milk amounts, not formula brands.
negative.prompt: Which formula brand is best, Similac or Enfamil?
